- FACTORY_PLAN default when unset: it has none and the driver refuses to run — factory-task line 73-74 and factory-wave line 98-99 both read: `if [ -z "${FACTORY_PLAN:-}" ]; then factory_die 2 "FACTORY_PLAN is unset — name the plan (FACTORY_PLAN=<plan.md> …) or launch through factory-dispatch"`.
- FACTORY-RESULT grammar accepted, and what is synthesised otherwise: accepted (ACCEPTED) is exactly a line with no `<` matching `FACTORY-RESULT[[:space:]]+status=(done|partial|failed)([[:space:]]|$)`, last such line wins (factory-task lines 230-238: "ACCEPTED is a line with no '<' matching the strict grammar `FACTORY-RESULT status=(done|partial|failed)` (the last one wins, as today)"). A NEAR-MISS — a line mentioning FACTORY-RESULT but not matching that grammar (colon after the label, `status:` instead of `status=`, an out-of-vocabulary status word, or markdown decoration) — is recorded verbatim (first 200 bytes, control bytes folded to space) as a synthesized `FACTORY-RESULT status=failed exit_code=$exit_code` / `FACTORY-CHECKS none=not-run` / `FACTORY-COMMITS 0` / `FACTORY-NOTES result-misparse: $near_note` (factory-task lines 232-234, 255-263). With no FACTORY-RESULT line at all, or when seat-submit itself failed, the driver synthesises the same failed/none/0 block with a NOTES line pointing at the log (factory-task lines 249-269).
- What factory-integrate merges, from where, and what it refuses: in `~/factory/base/<repo-name>` only, never touching `<repo-path>` itself, it creates/resets `integ/<run>` from `<repo-path>`'s current default branch, then `git merge --no-ff` each `task/<KEY>` in given order, fetching that branch from the key's own workspace clone first (factory-integrate header comment, lines 4-8). It refuses a key whose merge changed `docs/OPERATIONS.md` outside the `<!-- tasks:end -->` queue block, compared against the merge base — "the board (docs/OPERATIONS.md) is the orchestrator's to write … a change anywhere else in that file is refused" (factory-integrate lines 79-97); a refused/conflicted key leaves the tree incomplete (line 192 area) and it never runs the fast-forward itself, only prints the command (header comment lines 14-16).
- Where dispatch.log is written and the one line it holds: `$FACTORY_RUNS/<run>/dispatch.log`, created only on an actual launch (a dry run touches nothing) — factory-dispatch lines 183-187; the one line appended per launch is `factory-dispatch: run %s plan %s groups: %s\n` (line 189-190).
- What a hand launch must set: `FACTORY_PLAN` naming the plan file — both factory-task and factory-wave refuse (`factory_die 2`) without it (see above); the board's own RECIPES line gives the exact hand-launch invocation form: `FACTORY_PLAN=<plan>.md tools/factory/seat/factory-wave <run> <repo-path> "<KEY>"`.
